One-sentence judgment: career and technical education teachers (postsecondary) are not about 'explaining a craft once' — they convert the real work requirements of an industry field into trainable, operable, and assessable courses and practical training tasks at the career and technical education stage after high school graduation or leaving school, and are simultaneously responsible for learner operating safety, assessment standards, and training records. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Three (medium preparation, SVP 6.0 to below 7.0), with no Bright Outlook designation, and an interest code of SIR (social, investigative, realistic). The core boundary is: teaching and practical training qualifications must be obtained item by item according to local and institutional rules; learner assessment and completion determination, the conditions under which practical training equipment and sites may be used, and the handling of learner-protection matters are different responsibilities, and teachers cannot exceed their authority to replace the institution or competent authority in handling them.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to break real industry work processes into training tasks that learners can understand and do and be objectively assessed on, and to accept that the same operation must be demonstrated and corrected repeatedly for different ability levels (in the O*NET interest code, social is the highest at 94, and the work context shows 66% making a public speech every day, 68% in continuous contact with others, 75% indoors in a controlled environment every day, and 41% standing about half the time); you can spell out prohibited actions and protective requirements before learners use tools and equipment; you are willing to score against published standards and keep the original operating evidence, and to protect learners first and report per procedure when injury risk or an anomaly appears, rather than handling it yourself.

Conditions for pausing large investments first: you have not yet completed a full closed-loop exercise from training objectives and job task analysis to practical training safety plans to operating standards and scoring dimensions to records and feedback; or you are unwilling to record and report faithfully per policy, unwilling to repeatedly stress safety procedures while learners work, or unwilling to accept questions from peers and employers; also, having worked many years in an industry must not be treated as proof that you already have course design, practical training organization, and learner assessment ability.

Education, qualification, and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Three (medium preparation, SVP 6.0 to below 7.0), and the O*NET education survey shows 42% of respondents saying an associate degree or other two-year credential is needed, 20% a bachelor's degree, and 16% a postsecondary certificate; this occupation's page lists 33 certifications and no apprenticeship direction. In the United States, teaching and practical training authorization in public schools and vocational education institutions is determined by state and institutional rules, and industry certification usually cannot replace teacher qualification or institutional employment requirements. In mainland China, the corresponding teaching and practical training guidance qualifications must be obtained under the teacher qualification and vocational training systems and must meet institutional recruitment and employment conditions; qualification does not equal employment or the scope of fields that may be taught or approval for practical training projects and site equipment.

One sentence: this is a position that turns 'whether a learner has truly mastered an occupational or technical ability and has safely performed hands-on work' into reviewable evidence, with outputs being curriculum objectives and training plans, practical training safety plans, operating standards and scoring dimensions, learner performance and grade and attendance records, and exception and reporting records; it is not an institutional management or curriculum approval role, nor does it replace the institution's or competent authority's handling and reporting of learner-protection matters. For mainland China this route has not established occupation-level wage statistics that precisely correspond to this occupation, so this page publishes no figure and keeps the gap visible.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, technical course teaching (analyzing industry work requirements into training objectives and course content, lecturing and demonstrating and organizing learners' hands-on operation, and assessing against operating standards and giving feedback); second, practical training equipment and safety (supervising and checking learners' use of tools and equipment, maintaining and repairing laboratory equipment and tools, implementing protection and isolation requirements, and stopping use first and then reporting when a hazard is found); third, assessment and learner guidance (conducting oral and written and performance examinations, maintaining grade and attendance and training records, providing individualized instruction and tutoring, and advising on course choices and career decisions). All three share the same chain centered on real job requirements, operating safety, and learner evidence.
Technical course teaching

Analyze the target position's real work tasks and skill requirements → establish curriculum objectives and training plans and syllabi → prepare textbooks and teaching aids and practical training materials and design task contexts → lecture and demonstrate and organize learners' hands-on operation → assess against operating standards and observed performance and give improvement suggestions → record training activities and learner progress
Practical training equipment and safety

Editorial on organizing practical training: check equipment protection and sites before class, demonstrate and supervise, and record states; for Chinese university laboratory and practical training that is covered, Article 7 of the 2023 rules makes the project leader, including the course instructor, the first responsible person for project safety, the laboratory head the directly responsible person for that laboratory, and under Article 5 the school's party and administrative main leaders the first responsible person for the school; Article 10 requires safety training and assessment before admission and risk assessment for major hazard sources. Article 15 of the 2024 classification measures prohibits experiments while major hazards remain unrectified. Equipment repair and restoration follow the real division of personnel and procedures, and full repair authority is not automatically obtained from teacher status; other training institutions verify the applicable rules separately.

Administer oral and written and performance examinations and record results → observe learners' operations and assignments and score against published dimensions with the rationale stated → maintain detailed records of grades and attendance and training activities → provide individualized instruction and coaching and tutoring → advise on course choices and career decisions and academic problems → review registration applications and report exceptions as required and keep records

Editorial adjacent occupation comparison: CTE25-1194 teaches sub-baccalaureate post-high-school vocational training; training and development addresses organizational staff training, industrial and mechanical engineers and technicians focus on technical production and engineering support, and engineering higher education teachers teach engineering disciplines, with whether research is included depending on the actual position. Tasks and professional qualifications and hiring are verified separately, and it must not be generalized that adjacent positions do no teaching or that all higher education positions must do research.
Core purpose

Editorial summary: help learners acquire the target occupational skills, and observe learning performance through tasks, operating standards, and assessment records; course completion and ability records do not automatically confer an industry occupational qualification or guarantee employment.
Main subjects and basis

The subjects are learners after high school graduation or leaving school and in-service upskillers or career changers retraining, along with their class sections and small groups, as well as courses and training syllabi and textbooks, tools and equipment and protective equipment and laboratories and workshop sites, operating standards and examination plans and scoring rationale, detailed records of grades and attendance and training activities, and individualized instruction and tutoring and registration review materials; the basis is the local and institutional teaching and practical training guidance qualification requirements, the institution's and competent authority's course and program approval systems, industry and occupational standards and skill level requirements, equipment and site and material safety requirements, learner record and privacy and mandatory reporting requirements, and employers' hiring standards.
Core process

Analyze job tasks and training needs, design courses and training plans, prepare teaching aids and practical training materials, lecture and demonstrate, organize and supervise learner operations, assess against operating standards and give feedback, maintain training and grade records, provide individualized instruction and career guidance, and report exceptions as required.
Main outputs

Curriculum objectives and training syllabi and teaching materials, operating standards and examination plans and scoring rationale, detailed records of learner grades and attendance and training activities, equipment and tool maintenance and exception handling records, individualized instruction and tutoring and guidance records, registration review and communication records, and exception and reporting records.
Accountable parties

Teaching and laboratory and project safety follow the actual division of roles; for Chinese university laboratory and practical training that is covered, Article 7 of the 2023 rules makes the project leader, including the course instructor, the first responsible person for project safety, the laboratory head the directly responsible person for that laboratory, and under Article 5 the school's party and administrative main leaders the first responsible person for the school; Article 10 requires safety training and assessment before admission and risk assessment for major hazard sources. Article 15 of the 2024 classification measures prohibits experiments while major hazards remain unrectified. Equipment repair and restoration follow the real division of personnel and procedures, and full repair authority is not automatically obtained from teacher status; other training institutions verify the applicable rules separately. High school graduation or leaving school does not prove that all learners are adults. In China, if the position falls under a unit in close contact with minors and its staff, Article 11 of the Law on the Protection of Minors requires an immediate report to public security and civil affairs and education and other relevant departments upon harm or suspected harm or danger, and internal school reporting alone or waiting for teacher confirmation is not enough; adult learners are verified under the applicable law and the real institution's aid and reporting processes, and the editorial suggestion is to aid urgent injuries promptly without waiting for records or approval. The United States is verified separately under state law.
Qualification and authorization

In China, first distinguish higher vocational college teachers, other vocational school teachers, and training institution positions: Article 11 of the Teachers Law provides that higher education teacher qualification generally requires graduate or undergraduate graduation; Article 46 of the Vocational Education Law provides that specialized courses including practicum supervision require corresponding experience or practice and technical skills, that qualified industry personnel who pass educational and teaching ability training may serve full-time or part-time, and that the education requirement for specialized course teacher qualification may be lowered as appropriate, which must not be treated as automatic exemption from qualification. Specific certification and hiring and subject and facility division of labor are verified separately. In the United States, teaching is verified by state and institution and field taught for education and experience and applicable licensure; the BLS public school state licensure requirement cannot be expanded into a uniform license for all post-high-school private training institutions. For Chinese university laboratory and practical training that is covered, Article 7 of the 2023 rules makes the project leader, including the course instructor, the first responsible person for project safety, the laboratory head the directly responsible person for that laboratory, and under Article 5 the school's party and administrative main leaders the first responsible person for the school; Article 10 requires safety training and assessment before admission and risk assessment for major hazard sources. Article 15 of the 2024 classification measures prohibits experiments while major hazards remain unrectified. Equipment repair and restoration follow the real division of personnel and procedures, and full repair authority is not automatically obtained from teacher status; other training institutions verify the applicable rules separately. The United States is verified separately under state law.
Conclusion boundaries

Training records and assessment results describe how a learner performed under the given course and operating standards and training conditions; they are not a final characterization of the learner's occupational ability, nor do they replace the institution's and competent authority's handling of learner-protection matters, and they are updated as industry standards, equipment conditions, and training arrangements change; when citing, state the operating standard version, the assessment method, and the record period at the same time.

Before starting, verify at least six items: job duties (leaning toward technical course teaching, practical training equipment and safety, assessment and learner guidance, curriculum development and industry cooperation, or teaching research and institutional management), the required teaching and practical training guidance qualifications and the scope of fields that may be taught, the available tools and equipment and site conditions and the division of safety responsibility, class section and class hours and learner numbers and workload arrangements, learner grade and record and mandatory reporting requirements, and whether the role includes admissions review or school-enterprise cooperation or mentoring duties.
Occupational framing

This fixed identity 25-1194.00 mainly teaches sub-baccalaureate vocational training to people who have graduated from or left high school, and it cannot be equated with all higher education degree teachers, nor can a one-to-one Chinese classification be assumed from the name alone. JobZone3, with no Bright Outlook designation; industry 93% education / 7% other including government. Interest SIR: S94/I53/R46/C38/A36/E19; the specific interests teaching 94, public speaking 66, professional counseling 57, mechanical and electrical 41, and engineering 31 belong to a different set of dimensions and are not sub-items of social or individual competence thresholds.

The 1580 school program directory includes both the major taught and teacher training, and the number of graduates is not teacher educational attainment; the summary apprenticeship exploration entry lists no specific program. The 33 certifications include teaching and technical specification programs across fields and are not required of everyone. Methods and tools

The O*NET technology list names 14 categories of software skills, and the Hot Technologies page shows 6 items (Microsoft Office appears in 5% of job postings, Excel and PowerPoint 3% each, Outlook and Word 1% each, and Google Docs is given no share; the data source is 2025 U.S. job postings from Lightcast). The list indicates that the occupation may require office and teaching management software in hiring, with none of the shares high, and it does not indicate a proficiency threshold or that the position has been displaced. On-site methods and tools center on practical training tools and equipment and materials and protective equipment for each professional field, lecturing and demonstration and multimedia teaching aids, learning management and grade and attendance record systems, operating standards and examination plans and scoring rubrics, and courses and training syllabi and textbooks.
Safety and work permits

Work is mainly fixed in-institution schedules and practical training arrangements, while also carrying after-class workload such as lesson preparation and practical training preparation and grading and communication; the main load comes from long periods of speaking and demonstrating, continuous interpersonal interaction and coordination, and watching several learners' safety at once while they use tools and equipment in a laboratory or workshop. Pay and hours

U.S. 2025 median annual wage for this occupation is 63,820 USD, with an hourly wage of 30.68 USD; annual wage P10—P90 41,960—108,620 USD. U.S. 25-1194 postsecondary, sub-baccalaureate vocational training teachers: 2025 employment 123,100 → 2035 projection 122,700, a net change of about -400; the BLS Table 1.2 change rate is -0.3%, while the O*NET whole percentages show 0% (little or no change); 2025—2035 average annual openings 8,000 (including replacement needs, not net new). This identity teaches post-high-school, sub-baccalaureate vocational training and is not all higher education teachers; high school graduation or leaving school does not mean all learners are adults. Career and technical education teachers (postsecondary) (O*NET-SOC 25-1194.00, Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary) teach at the career and technical education stage after high school graduation or leaving school, covering vocational courses in fields such as construction, mechanics and repair, manufacturing, transportation, and cosmetology and barbering, for learners who have already graduated from or left high school and aim to obtain an occupational qualification or work in technical jobs; the teaching takes place in public or private institutions whose main business is degree education or vocational education. Daily work includes: observing and evaluating learners' assignments and operations to judge progress, providing feedback, and giving improvement suggestions; using visual aids such as charts, drawings, videos, and slides to lecture and organize discussions in order to improve learners' knowledge and abilities; supervising and checking learners' use of tools and equipment; administering oral, written, or performance examinations to measure progress and evaluate training effectiveness; providing individualized instruction, coaching, and tutoring; preparing reports and maintaining records of learner grades, attendance, and training activity details; developing courses and planning teaching content and methods; determining the training needs of learners or employees; supervising independent or group projects, field internships, laboratory work, or other training; integrating academic and vocational courses so learners gain a variety of skills; selecting and assembling books, materials, supplies, and equipment for training, courses, or projects; conducting on-the-job training courses or training sessions, teaching and demonstrating the principles, techniques, processes, and methods of assigned subjects; purchasing, maintaining, and repairing laboratory equipment and tools; writing course syllabi and training schedules and establishing course objectives; advising learners on course choices, career decisions, and other academic and career issues; attending meetings, seminars, and training to follow field developments and integrate relevant information into training programs; developing instructional software, multimedia teaching aids, or learning materials; participating in faculty and institutional committees related to budgets, curriculum revision, and course and certificate requirements; arranging for experts in related fields to lecture at the school; and reviewing registration applications and contacting applicants for additional information. It carries responsibility for learner protection and teaching quality and teaching scope, but does not replace the institution's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and the handling of learner-protection matters and personnel management.

paragraphs: This page compares career and technical education teachers (postsecondary) with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is a better fit for. Adjacent directions are described by their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean that job titles or teaching and practical training qualifications are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational direction and core outputs are based on O*NET-SOC 25-1194.00 and the official descriptions of adjacent entries (U.S. framing); the adjacent occupations listed by this evidence route are training and development specialists, industrial engineers, mechanical engineers, industrial engineering technologists and technicians, and mechanical engineering technologists and technicians, with engineering teachers (higher education) as a related O*NET occupation; teaching and practical training guidance qualifications, the scope of fields that may be taught, learner assessment and completion determination, and the handling and reporting authority for learner-protection matters must be verified separately under each jurisdiction and institutional policy; this page does not present any direction as a shortcut for switching careers.

The table below compares the differences in duties and outputs between career and technical education teachers (postsecondary) and adjacent directions; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the job titles sound.

Training and development specialists usually serve in-service employees inside an enterprise, and results are measured by business performance and job competence improvement; this occupation serves learners at the post-high-school career and technical education stage and carries responsibility for the curriculum system and operating standards and grades and attendance and completion requirements.

If you would rather do in-service training and organizational capability improvement inside an enterprise, examine the training and development specialist direction first; if you would rather carry responsibility for the curriculum system and practical training teaching and learner assessment, examine this occupation first.
Designing and delivering training for in-service staff to improve job competence, with outputs mainly training plans and learning effectiveness evaluation.
Training and development specialists

Industrial engineers design and improve production and service systems themselves and do not carry teaching or assessment responsibility; this occupation converts industry work requirements into training objectives and practical training tasks and is responsible for learner operating safety and ability determination.

If you would rather design and improve process and system efficiency, examine the industrial engineer direction first; if you would rather convert technical requirements into courses and practical training and lead learners to produce them, examine this occupation first.
Designing and improving the processes, people, and resource allocation of production and service systems, with outputs mainly system plans and efficiency indicators.
Industrial engineers

Mechanical engineers center on the design, analysis, and verification of mechanical products, with results measured by technical indicators; this occupation centers on teaching mechanical and repair vocational courses and organizing practical training, and its product is learner competence evidence.

If you would rather design and analyze mechanical products, examine the mechanical engineer direction first; if you would rather teach and lead practical training in the mechanical and repair field, examine this occupation first.
Designing and analyzing mechanical products and components, with outputs mainly drawings and technical plans and test conclusions.
Mechanical engineers

Industrial engineering technologists and technicians carry engineering support and technical execution work, usually under an engineer's direction; this occupation independently carries course and practical training teaching and learner assessment, and the subjects of responsibility are learner competence and training safety.

If you would rather do engineering support and data and process execution, examine the industrial engineering technologist and technician direction first; if you would rather teach classes independently and lead practical training, examine this occupation first.
Providing measurement, data collection, and process support for industrial engineering plans, with outputs mainly process documents and measurement data.
Industrial engineering technologists and technicians

Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians focus on assembling and repairing and testing equipment and components themselves, and the served object is equipment; this occupation focuses on teaching and practical training guidance for mechanical and repair courses, and the served object is learners, while also carrying teaching and assessment responsibility.

If you would rather assemble and commission and repair mechanical equipment itself, examine the mechanical engineering technologist and technician direction first; if you would rather teach mechanical repair ability to learners and be responsible for practical training safety, examine this occupation first.
Carrying assembly, commissioning and repair, and test support for mechanical equipment, with outputs mainly repair and commissioning records and test data.
Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians

Engineering teachers (higher education) carry degree course teaching and research, teach undergraduates and graduate students, usually require an advanced degree, and produce academic results; this occupation serves vocational and technical training not aimed at a degree, with the focus on operating ability and job-entry qualifications, and usually has industry hands-on experience as the entry point.

If you would rather do engineering discipline teaching and research in a university, examine the engineering teacher (higher education) direction first; if you would rather do practical training teaching for career and technical education learners, examine this occupation first.
Teaching engineering disciplines and conducting research in higher education degree courses, with outputs mainly course teaching and academic results.

In the United States, teaching is verified by state and institution and field taught for education and experience and applicable licensure; the BLS public school state licensure requirement cannot be expanded into a uniform license for all post-high-school private training institutions.

Equipment repair and restoration follow the real division of personnel and procedures, and full repair authority is not automatically obtained from teacher status; other training institutions verify the applicable rules separately.

entries.answer: Teaching vocational courses at the career and technical education stage after high school graduation or leaving school: observing and evaluating learners' assignments and operations to judge progress and providing feedback and improvement suggestions; using visual aids such as charts and drawings and videos and slides to lecture and organize discussions; supervising and checking learners' use of tools and equipment; administering oral and written or performance examinations to measure progress and evaluate training effectiveness; providing individualized instruction and coaching and tutoring; preparing reports and maintaining detailed records of learner grades and attendance and training activities; developing courses and planning teaching content and methods; determining the training needs of learners or employees; supervising independent or group projects and field internships and laboratory work; integrating academic and vocational courses; selecting and assembling books and materials and supplies and equipment; conducting on-the-job training and demonstrating the principles and technical processes and methods of assigned subjects; purchasing and maintaining and repairing laboratory equipment and tools; writing course syllabi and training schedules and establishing course objectives; advising learners on course choices and career decisions; attending meetings and seminars and training; developing teaching aids; participating in faculty and institutional committees; arranging for experts to lecture at the school; and reviewing registration applications.
entries.question: What does a career and technical education teacher (postsecondary) do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks include learner safety risk when using tools and equipment in practical training, leakage of learner records and personal information, assessing only the finished product and inconsistent scoring standards, bringing occupational and gender or background stereotypes into teaching and tracking recommendations, handling learner-protection matters beyond one's authority or delaying reports, and going beyond authorization and skill depreciation under industry technology updates; control depends on pre-class risk assessment and checklist checks and personal protection and isolation requirements and continuous circulation and correction and minimizing learner data and dual operating standard and process evidence assessment and clear escalation paths and continuous teaching research.
entries.question: What risks does this work most need to watch for in advance?

entries.answer: The fit signals are being able to convert real industry work tasks into training tasks that learners can understand and do and be objectively assessed on, being willing to manage operating safety and individual differences at the same time at the laboratory and practical training site, and being able to give feedback using operating evidence rather than impressions; what matters is whether you have reviewable course and training syllabi and practical training supervision and safety records and scoring rationale and actual teaching performance, not just an interest in a craft or industry experience.
entries.question: How do I judge whether this work suits me?

entries.answer: Steps such as job task data retrieval and organizing, first drafts of courseware and training materials, first drafts of test items and performance exam scoring sheets, grade and attendance and training ledger organizing, and notice and communication text drafting can be assisted; whether tasks match current industry requirements and whether demonstrations are accurate and whether learners meet the operating conditions and whether scoring is fair and the reporting of learner-protection matters are still verified and borne by a qualified teacher.
entries.question: Which steps will AI and automation change?

entries.answer: Judgments about the alignment of training objectives with current industry requirements, demonstration accuracy, on-site circulation during learners' hands-on work and decisions to stop use, operating standards and assessment conclusions and grade changes, the basis and limits of completion and tracking recommendations, the records and time limits for learner records and reporting, and consistency checks between automated scoring results and original operating evidence must all be completed by authorized people with a paper trail.
entries.question: Which steps must keep human checks?

subject.summary: This page's entry corresponds to career and technical education teachers (postsecondary) (O*NET-SOC 25-1194.00, Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary): teaching vocational courses in fields such as construction and mechanical and repair and manufacturing and transportation and cosmetology and barbering at the career and technical education stage after high school graduation or leaving school — converting real job tasks into training objectives and a course syllabus, preparing teaching aids and practical training materials, using visual aids to lecture and organize discussions, supervising and checking learners' use of tools and equipment, administering oral and written and performance examinations and observing learners' operations, providing individualized instruction and coaching and tutoring, maintaining detailed records of learner grades and attendance and training activities, developing courses and planning teaching content and methods, and advising learners on course choices and career decisions; work is mainly fixed in-institution schedules and practical training arrangements (75% indoors in a controlled environment every day, 68% in continuous contact with others, 66% making a public speech every day, 41% standing about half the time, 32% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of others), and its duties do not replace the institution's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and personnel management, with learner-protection matters handled by designated positions per policy.
